description: Change a saved Request only as the user asked: its conditions, quantities or price policy; never widen it on your own. Send only the fields the user asked to change and omit every other one: omitted fields stay as they are. Leave raw_request out of a quantity or term change; when the user now wants different items, send their new words as raw_request with need_option_changes (see its field). Use need_quantity_changes for existing Need quantities (conditions_confirmed=true attests the whole Need, its quantity, options and hard terms: pass it with a quantity the user asked for only if they have also confirmed the rest; otherwise the Need becomes unconfirmed and you ask them), or need_term_changes for selected warranty/returns/authorized-seller requirements. Use need_option_changes to replace one existing Need's complete acceptable-option set, optionally its description; it does not append or select options. An empty option set is unresolved. Replacement defaults conditions_confirmed to false; set true only with current user authority for these exact options. Targeted changes may combine, never with purchase_spec. To change a multi-item Request's basket answer (basket_acceptance), send the complete purchase_spec with everything else unchanged; its max total is the pricing_policy or a confirmed basket all-in ceiling. Moving all_required to partial_allowed is the user's own choice, never yours. Omitted terms stay unchanged; explicit null removes that condition. A changed quantity or hard-term set resets conditions_confirmed unless that change explicitly supplies conditions_confirmed=true under current user instructions. Soft confirmation is not payment authority. Every targeted edit preserves ceilings and other Needs. Read a current Need section before an ambiguous edit. Preserve intent identity and acquisition source. Pass the current version; on conflict read and ask/reconcile. No inferred reservation price. To add the delivery postal code, send the complete destination with postal_code; it is checked against the Request country and sets the derived state. Optional request_format=overview returns an incomplete bounded receipt; full remains the default.

changes.description: The fields to change, with expected_version.

postal_code.description: Delivery postal code: a US ZIP (12345 or 12345-6789) or a 7-digit Israeli postal code, checked against the Request country (postal_code_invalid otherwise). Optional when saving; required before an Offer can be prepared. The region (US state code) is derived from it.

region.description: State or region. Derived from postal_code when one is given; otherwise a state name or two-letter code is stored as the state code.

exact_items.description: Key options the person agreed to (brand+model+variant, or link). source_text: their words, one model per line. Authority as confirm_future_purchase_item.

may_commit.description: Declared "may commit". true records that the user states (directly, or by instructing you) that they are ready to buy from an Offer that fits this Request; false withdraws it. Omit to keep it. Popular Demand records who declared it and when; it is never a permission Popular Demand grants or verifies. It was declared for the current conditions, so any other change to them (words, products, Needs, ceilings, price policy, destination or timing) withdraws it unless the same edit sends true again. Only set true on the user's actual instruction.

need_option_changes.description: Replace the complete acceptable-option set of an existing stable Need, optionally its description. This does not append or select options. An empty list means unresolved. Defaults conditions_confirmed to false; true requires current user authority for these exact options. Preserves other Needs, quantities, hard terms and every ceiling. May combine with targeted quantity/term changes and raw_request, never with purchase_spec. Changing raw_request unconfirms the other Needs.

need_quantity_changes.description: Change quantities of existing stable Need IDs without replacing the basket. Use either this field or purchase_spec, never both. Null means unknown. Does not multiply ceilings. A changed quantity resets Need confirmation unless conditions_confirmed=true explicitly attests current user instructions for that exact Need. Soft confirmation grants no purchase/payment authority.

conditions_confirmed.description: True attests actual current user instructions for this exact changed Need, including quantity, acceptable options and hard terms. It is soft demand, never purchase or payment authority. Omission resets confirmation on a material change.

need_term_changes.description: Change selected warranty_months_min, returns_days_min or authorized_seller_required fields of existing stable Need IDs. Omitted fields remain unchanged; null removes only that condition. Preserves quantities, alternatives and ceilings. A changed term set resets Need confirmation unless conditions_confirmed=true explicitly attests current user instructions for that exact Need. May combine with need_quantity_changes, never with purchase_spec. Requires actual user authority.

conditions_confirmed.description: True attests actual current user instructions for this exact changed Need, including quantity, acceptable options and hard terms. It is soft demand, never purchase or payment authority. Omission resets confirmation on a material change.

policy_confirmed.description: true attests the user's current instructions for the resulting price policy; false clears confirmation. Omit to apply the narrowing rule above.

pricing_policy.description: Replace the price policy. A same or narrower policy (lower explicit ceiling, larger required saving, or explore) keeps the existing confirmation. A wider or different-mode policy clears it unless policy_confirmed=true attests the user's current instructions. Ask the user before widening their stated price limit. Confirmation records provenance, not spending authority.

raw_request.description: The user's own words for the wish, only when the wish itself changed: they reworded it, or they now want different items (send it with need_option_changes). Omit it for a quantity or term change. A reworded raw_request unconfirms every Need except those whose options this change replaces, which follow that change's conditions_confirmed.

request_format.description: Full is the default. Overview is incomplete: it preserves current conditions identity, price scopes and Need quantities, but omits Need descriptions, hard terms, alternatives and root product fields. Read the selected Need section before an ambiguous edit.

request_key.description: Your key for this change; the same key repeats it safely.

user_confirmed.description: True: the user said yes to this exact change.

name: update_future_purchase

may_commit_declared_at.description: When the owner or their agent declared that the owner is ready to buy from an Offer if one fits; null when not declared. A recorded statement, never a permission Popular Demand grants or verifies.

questions_emailed.description: Whether questions about this Request are emailed to the user. False while email updates for it are off: tell the user they could miss an offer, and answer questions you receive.

possible_duplicate_of.description: Open Requests of the same owner that closely match this new one: the same exact product references, the same top Need option set or the same words, with an overlapping destination. The new Request was saved anyway. If one is the same purchase, update or close the extra Request so the user is counted once.

result.description: The Request after the change: the fields to act on are listed here. The result is the full Request (or its overview, as request_format chose); get_future_purchase lists its full shape.

title: Update a Request
